newsitem.title: USA: Groups sue to protect Hawaiian plants' habitat.
newsitem.headline: Groups sue to protect Hawaiian plants' habitat.

text.p: Three conservation groups said Wednesday they sued the Interior Department to try to force it to designate critical habitat in Hawaii to save 278 species of endangered and threatened plants.
The Fish and Wildlife Service, an agency of the Interior Department, listed the plants under the Endangered Species Act, but in most cases did not designated habitat to be protected for the plants.

"By listing plant species without protecting their habitat, the Fish and Wildlife Service has lost sight of an important purpose of the Endangered Species Act, protecting the ecosystems that all Hawaiian species need to survive and flourish," William Sager, chairman of the Conservation Council of Hawaii, said in a statement.
That is Hawaii's affiliate of the National Wildlife Federation. The Sierra Club and the Hawaiian Botanical Society also were parties to the lawsuit.

The groups said that 282 Hawaiian plants have been listed as endangered or threatened, but the Fish and Wildlife Service has only designated critical habitat for three of them. Another was listed before the habitat designation requirement.

"Ninety percent of Hawaii's plants are found nowhere else in the world, and 10 percent of Hawaii's plants are already known to be extinct," said Wisteria Loeffler, president of the Hawaii Botanical Society.
